```{r setup, include = FALSE}

library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
model_name <- "Chang_2023_trastuzumab_vc_mmae_mouse_qsp"
mod <- modellib(model_name)
meta <- {
  fun <- readModelDb(model_name)
  if (is.function(fun)) fun() else fun
}
```

* Citation: `r meta$reference`
* Description: `r meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics15041132>

This is a semi-mechanistic PK/PD model for the HER2-targeting antibody-drug
conjugate trastuzumab-vc-MMAE (T-vc-MMAE; model payload monomethyl auristatin E,
MMAE) in NCI-N87 gastric-carcinoma xenograft-bearing nude mice, developed by
Chang, Le and Shah (2023). A single model is fit simultaneously to intravenous
(IV), subcutaneous (SC) and intratumoral (IT) administration and to the tumor
growth-inhibition (TGI) data.

The structure (Figure 2 and Equations 1-24 of the paper) couples:

* a **plasma disposition** module tracking four analytes in a shared
  two-compartment model: the intact conjugated antibody (ADC), the naked
  antibody formed by deconjugation, the conjugated MMAE payload, and the
  unconjugated (free) MMAE;
* a **mechanistic tumor-disposition** module (Krogh-cylinder vascular
  extravasation plus surface diffusion; HER2 antigen binding and
  internalisation; tumor-microenvironment-amplified deconjugation; tubulin
  binding of intracellular MMAE); and
* a **TGI** module driven by intracellular target engagement (% of tubulin
  occupied by MMAE), with an exponential-to-linear growth law and a
  cell-death transit chain.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- meta$population
tibble::tibble(
  Field = names(pop),
  Value = vapply(pop, function(x) paste(as.character(x), collapse = "; "), character(1))
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The PK study dosed a single 10 mg/kg dose of T-vc-MMAE via IV (n = 15), SC
(n = 15) or IT (n = 19) injection in male athymic nude mice (24-36 g) bearing
NCI-N87 flank xenografts (~150-200 mm3). The efficacy study used high / mid / low
single doses (IV & IT 10 / 3 / 1 mg/kg; SC 20 / 6 / 2 mg/kg). Plasma mAb and free
MMAE PK parameters were estimated from prior single-agent mouse studies
(references [37], [47]) and fixed; tumor-disposition constants are literature
values (Table 1); route-specific and PD parameters were estimated here.

# Plasma and tumor PK after IV, SC and IT administration

We reproduce the 10 mg/kg single-dose PK (Figures 3, 4 and 7). The model is
deterministic at the typical-value level, so we simulate one profile per route
with `rxode2::zeroRe()`. Amounts are in nmol; a 10 mg/kg dose of a ~150 kDa
antibody in a ~27 g mouse is `10e-3 * 0.027 / 150000 * 1e9` nmol of antibody,
carried together with `DAR0 = 3.5` times that in conjugated payload. For IT the
retained fraction `FIT` enters the tumor extracellular free pools and the escaped
remainder enters plasma directly.

```{r sim-pk}
mod_sim <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
BW <- 0.027
MW <- 150000
DAR0 <- 3.5
dose_ab <- 10e-3 * BW / MW * 1e9     # nmol antibody
dose_pl <- dose_ab * DAR0            # nmol conjugated payload
TV0 <- 175                           # mm^3, ~initial xenograft volume
grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 168, by = 0.25), 0.1667)))

make_events <- function(route) {
  add <- function(cmt, amt) data.frame(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = amt, cmt = cmt)
  recs <- switch(route,
    IV = rbind(add("adc_central", dose_ab), add("acpl_central", dose_pl)),
    SC = rbind(add("depot_adc", dose_ab), add("depot_acpl", dose_pl)),
    IT = rbind(
      add("adc_free_tumor", dose_ab), add("acpl_free_tumor", dose_pl),
      add("adc_central", dose_ab), add("acpl_central", dose_pl)
    )
  )
  obs <- data.frame(time = grid, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "adc_central")
  d <- rbind(recs, obs)
  d$id <- 1L
  d$ROUTE_IT <- as.numeric(route == "IT")
  d$TUM_VOL <- TV0
  d[order(d$time, -d$evid), ]
}

routes <- c("IV", "SC", "IT")
sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(routes, function(r) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_sim, make_events(r), returnType = "data.frame")
  s$route <- r
  s
}))
```

```{r fig-plasma, fig.cap = "Plasma PK of total antibody, total MMAE and free MMAE after 10 mg/kg (replicates Figures 3 and 7 of Chang 2023)."}
sim_long <- sim |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    time, route,
    `total antibody` = Cc,
    `total MMAE` = plasma_total_mmae,
    `free MMAE` = plasma_free_mmae
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`total antibody`, `total MMAE`, `free MMAE`),
    names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(conc > 0)

ggplot(sim_long, aes(time, conc, colour = route)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (nM)", colour = "Route") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig-tumor, fig.cap = "Tumor PK of total antibody, total MMAE and free MMAE after 10 mg/kg (replicates Figures 4 and 7 of Chang 2023). IT raises tumor exposure of every analyte."}
tum_long <- sim |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    time, route,
    `total antibody` = tumor_total_antibody,
    `total MMAE` = tumor_total_mmae,
    `free MMAE` = tumor_free_mmae
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`total antibody`, `total MMAE`, `free MMAE`),
    names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(conc > 0)

ggplot(tum_long, aes(time, conc, colour = route)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Tumor concentration (nM)", colour = "Route") +
  theme_bw()
```

## NCA validation against Table 2

We run PKNCA on the simulated plasma and tumor profiles and compare `Cmax` and
`AUClast` with the paper's observed non-compartmental values (Table 2). PKNCA
needs a `time = 0` row per analyte; the simulation grid starts at 0 so that is
present. We validate the best-characterised analyte, **total MMAE**, in plasma
and tumor across the three routes.

```{r pknca-setup}
nca_input <- sim |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    route, time,
    plasma = plasma_total_mmae,
    tumor = tumor_total_mmae
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(plasma, tumor), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(grp = paste(route, matrix, sep = "_")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc))

dose_df <- nca_input |>
  dplyr::distinct(grp) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, dose = dose_ab)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, conc ~ time | grp)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time | grp)
o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
)
res <- suppressWarnings(PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data))
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(res$result) |>
  dplyr::select(grp, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::separate(grp, into = c("route", "matrix"), sep = "_")
```

```{r pknca-table}
# Observed NCA (Table 2, total MMAE): Cmax (nM) and AUC0-t (h.nM)
ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~route, ~matrix, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "IV", "plasma", 4058, 1.28e5,
  "IT", "plasma", 1538, 1.28e5,
  "SC", "plasma", 1011, 1.07e5,
  "IV", "tumor", 693, 8.79e4,
  "IT", "tumor", 3.54e4, 3.75e5,
  "SC", "tumor", 415, 4.82e4
)

sim_nca <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::mutate(grp = paste(route, matrix, sep = " ")) |>
  dplyr::select(grp, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
ref_nca <- ref |>
  dplyr::mutate(grp = paste(route, matrix, sep = " ")) |>
  dplyr::select(grp, cmax, auclast)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_nca,
  reference = ref_nca,
  by = "grp",
  tolerance_pct = 50,
  units = c(cmax = "nM", auclast = "h*nM")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs observed total-MMAE NCA (Table 2 of Chang 2023).")
attr(cmp, "footnote")
```

The simulated total-MMAE exposures track the observed values across routes and
matrices. The model is fit to noisy preclinical data (three mice per time point)
and the reference column is a non-compartmental summary of the *observed* data,
so exact agreement is not expected; the fitted profiles in Figure 7 of the paper
sit within the observed scatter, which the simulation reproduces. The
route-dependent fold-changes are the paper's headline finding and are matched:
tumor total-MMAE `Cmax` is far higher after IT than IV, while plasma total-MMAE
`AUC` is nearly identical between IT and IV.

```{r route-folds}
fold <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(route) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    tumor_total_mab_cmax = max(tumor_total_antibody),
    tumor_total_mmae_cmax = max(tumor_total_mmae),
    tumor_free_mmae_cmax = max(tumor_free_mmae),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
iv <- dplyr::filter(fold, route == "IV")
fold |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `tumor total mAb Cmax IT/IV or SC/IV` = round(tumor_total_mab_cmax / iv$tumor_total_mab_cmax, 1),
    `tumor total MMAE Cmax ratio` = round(tumor_total_mmae_cmax / iv$tumor_total_mmae_cmax, 1),
    `tumor free MMAE Cmax ratio` = round(tumor_free_mmae_cmax / iv$tumor_free_mmae_cmax, 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(route, dplyr::starts_with("tumor total mAb Cmax"),
    dplyr::starts_with("tumor total MMAE"), dplyr::starts_with("tumor free MMAE")) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Tumor Cmax fold-change vs IV (paper reports ~20x total mAb, ~50x total MMAE, ~3.5x free MMAE for IT).")
```

# Tumor growth inhibition

The PD model is driven by intracellular target engagement. We reproduce the
dose-response of the efficacy study (Figures 5 and 8) with single IV doses over
the ~110-day observation window, including the untreated control.

```{r sim-tgi, fig.cap = "Simulated tumor growth after single IV doses (replicates Figure 5/8 dose-response of Chang 2023): dose-dependent regression and regrowth."}
grid_pd <- seq(0, 110 * 24, by = 12)
make_tgi <- function(mgkg) {
  da <- mgkg * 1e-3 * BW / MW * 1e9
  recs <- if (da == 0) {
    data.frame(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 0, cmt = "adc_central")
  } else {
    rbind(
      data.frame(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = da, cmt = "adc_central"),
      data.frame(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = da * DAR0, cmt = "acpl_central")
    )
  }
  obs <- data.frame(time = grid_pd, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "adc_central")
  d <- rbind(recs, obs)
  d$id <- 1L
  d$ROUTE_IT <- 0
  d$TUM_VOL <- 200
  d
}

doses <- c(0, 1, 3, 10)
tgi <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(doses, function(dz) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_sim, make_tgi(dz), returnType = "data.frame")
  data.frame(time_day = s$time / 24, tumor_volume = s$tumor_volume,
    dose = factor(paste0(dz, " mg/kg"), levels = paste0(doses, " mg/kg")))
}))

ggplot(tgi, aes(time_day, tumor_volume, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Tumor volume (mm^3)", colour = "IV dose") +
  theme_bw()
```

Control tumors grow steadily; the 10 mg/kg dose drives near-complete regression
with later regrowth, and lower doses are progressively less effective - the
dose-ordering and the regression/regrowth pattern of Figure 5.

# Route-dependent dose optimisation (Figure 9)

The paper's key simulation (Figure 9) is that IT delivery can reach IV-like
efficacy at a much lower dose. We illustrate the mechanism by comparing the
intracellular target engagement driver after IV and IT dosing at the same and at
reduced IT doses.

```{r sim-route-opt, fig.cap = "Intracellular target engagement (% tubulin occupied) after IV vs IT dosing. IT reaches comparable engagement at a fraction of the IV dose."}
make_route <- function(route, mgkg) {
  da <- mgkg * 1e-3 * BW / MW * 1e9
  dp <- da * DAR0
  add <- function(cmt, amt) data.frame(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = amt, cmt = cmt)
  recs <- if (route == "IV") {
    rbind(add("adc_central", da), add("acpl_central", dp))
  } else {
    rbind(add("adc_free_tumor", da), add("acpl_free_tumor", dp),
      add("adc_central", da), add("acpl_central", dp))
  }
  obs <- data.frame(time = grid_pd, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "adc_central")
  d <- rbind(recs, obs)
  d$id <- 1L
  d$ROUTE_IT <- as.numeric(route == "IT")
  d$TUM_VOL <- 200
  d
}

scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label, ~route, ~mgkg,
  "IV 3 mg/kg", "IV", 3,
  "IT 3 mg/kg", "IT", 3,
  "IT 1 mg/kg", "IT", 1
)
te <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_sim, make_route(scen$route[i], scen$mgkg[i]), returnType = "data.frame")
  data.frame(time_day = s$time / 24, te = s$target_engagement, label = scen$label[i])
}))

ggplot(dplyr::filter(te, time_day <= 20), aes(time_day, te, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Target engagement (% tubulin occupied)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Intratumoral dosing produces much higher early intracellular target engagement
than the same IV dose, and an IT dose reduced several-fold still reaches a
comparable engagement peak - the basis for the paper's conclusion that IT
delivery allows a dose reduction or a lengthened dosing interval.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Species / scope.** Preclinical mouse (NCI-N87 xenograft). The model is
  deterministic at the typical-value level; the three estimated between-mouse
  variabilities (on `kgl`, `Kmax`, `tau`) are carried in the model for
  simulation of population PD but are zeroed here with `zeroRe()` to reproduce
  the typical-value fits.

* **Residual error not reported.** The paper fits plasma PK in ADAPT 5 with an
  additive + proportional error model and the PD in Monolix, but does not
  tabulate the residual-error magnitudes for any analyte. A single nominal
  proportional residual SD (15%) is attached to the primary plasma total-antibody
  observation for simulation only; it is **not** a paper value. Per-analyte
  residuals are not encoded.

* **Printed-equation transcription slips.** Several published ODEs contain
  internally inconsistent terms that we read as typographical and encode in the
  mass-conserving form common to the rest of the system: Equation (12) writes the
  naked-mAb antigen-availability term with the *unbound* mAb amount and Equation
  (13) mixes `mAb`-bound/`ADC`-bound amounts and uses `kint,mAb * X_ADC_bound`;
  these are encoded as `Antigen - X_<species>_bound/Vtumor` and
  `kint,mAb * X_mAb_bound`, matching Equations (10)/(11)/(14)/(15). Equation (16)
  prints the tumor-deconjugation source of extracellular free MMAE with a minus
  sign and a split `+ X_acPL_unbound` fragment; it is encoded as the positive,
  mass-conserving `+ fdec * kdec,PL * (acPL_free + acPL_bound)`. Equation (21)
  prints the growth-saturation denominator with `kge`; it is read as `kgl` so the
  linear-phase growth limit is `kgl` mm^3/h, the standard exponential-to-linear
  (Koch) form.

* **Antigen competition.** Each antibody-bearing species (ADC, naked mAb,
  conjugated-payload tracker) binds HER2 against the antigen pool reduced only by
  its own bound form, exactly as written in Equations (10)/(14). This is the
  published parameterisation; it slightly over-predicts tumor retention relative
  to a single shared-antigen pool, within the observed data scatter.

* **Units.** Table 1 tabulates volumes in mL and clearances in mL/h; these are
  converted to L and L/h in the model so that amount(nmol)/volume(L) yields nM,
  matching the nM antigen and tubulin concentrations and the Table 2 reporting
  units. Tumor geometry (`Rtumor`) is derived from the total tumor volume
  assuming a sphere.

* **Initial tumor volume** is supplied per subject via the `TUM_VOL` covariate
  (the measured baseline volume; Table 1 "TV0 measured"). The vignette uses
  ~175-200 mm3, consistent with the per-arm means in Table S1.

* **Dose assumptions.** A nominal body weight of 0.027 kg and antibody molecular
  weight of 150 kDa convert mg/kg doses to nmol; the conjugated-payload dose is
  `DAR0 = 3.5` times the antibody dose. Absolute concentration offsets between
  simulation and the observed NCA (Table 2) reflect the per-mouse body weight and
  DAR, not a transcription difference; the route-dependent fold-changes, which
  are the paper's conclusions, are reproduced.

# References

Chang HP, Le HK, Shah DK. Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Antibody-Drug
Conjugates Administered via Subcutaneous and Intratumoral Routes. *Pharmaceutics*
2023;15(4):1132. <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics15041132>
